title: Production releases
summary: How changes reach production safely: approved, built by the pipeline, rolled out gradually and with a way back.
scope: Every release of an application or infrastructure change to production. Changes to development and test environments are out of scope.

requirements.title: Every release has an approved change record
requirements.statement: A release to production starts only after its change record is approved, and the change number is recorded with the deployment.
requirements.rationale: During an incident the first question is what changed. The change records answer it.
guidance: Follow the process 'Release a service to production'.
Put the change number in the description of the deployment run.

verification.description: The production deployment step refuses to start without an approved change number.

requirements.title: Only pipeline-built images
requirements.statement: Only container images built and signed by the company build pipeline are deployed to production.
requirements.rationale: An image built on a laptop cannot be traced to reviewed code and may contain anything.
guidance: Use the shared build workflow; it signs every image it builds.
Refer to images by digest or by the version the pipeline gave them.

lookFor: An image reference with the tag latest in a production manifest
An image from a registry other than the company artifact registry

requirements.title: A tested way back
requirements.statement: Every release has a written rollback plan, and database changes can be undone or are compatible with the previous version.
requirements.rationale: Rolling back is the fastest fix for a bad release, but only if it works.
guidance: Write the previous image version in the change record.
Split database changes: first add, release, then remove in a later release.

verification.description: Checked by the change manager and in code review.

lookFor: A migration that drops or renames a column used by the current version
A migration with no down step

requirements.title: Gradual roll-out for critical services
requirements.statement: Releases of critical services go to a small share of traffic first and to everyone only when the error rate stays normal.
requirements.rationale: A bad release then hurts 10% of customers for 15 minutes instead of all of them.
guidance: Turn on the canary roll-out in your Argo CD application.
Keep the automatic stop on error rate switched on.

verification.description: Platform policy check on the Argo CD application.

requirements.title: No releases during a change freeze
requirements.statement: No release is planned during a change freeze, except to fix an incident.
requirements.rationale: Freezes cover the busiest days, when an incident costs the most.
guidance: Check the change freeze calendar before planning a release.

verification.description: The change manager rejects changes inside a freeze.

requirements.title: Hide unfinished work behind feature flags
requirements.statement: Teams may release unfinished features switched off behind a feature flag instead of keeping long-lived branches.
requirements.rationale: Small, frequent releases are easier to roll back than big ones.

lookFor: A feature flag with no owner or removal date in its definition
